title: Constant scalar restriction preserves tensor, total complexes and K-flat localization
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], with exact abelian sheafification and the sheafified tensor structures [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $R=\underline B$ its constant ring sheaf, and $\iota:B^{\mathrm{pre}}\to R$ its sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $C_B:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ be restriction to constant scalar sections [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], with the canonical inverse extending scalar actions locally. It is an additive exact symmetric monoidal equivalence for the ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and sheafified objectwise $\otimes_B$, with natural comparisons
$$C_B(M\otimes_R N)\cong C_B(M)\otimes_B C_B(N),\qquad C_B(R)\cong\underline B.$$
Both tensor maps send each local pure tensor to the same pure tensor, and the unit comparison sends the image of each constant scalar to itself. These maps commute with associators, unitors and symmetry. Termwise they give natural isomorphisms of signed direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and preserve and reflect flatness and K-flatness. Here flatness means exactness of tensor with the object, and K-flatness means acyclicity after total tensor with every acyclic complex; equivalently both total tensor functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For ordinary unbounded K-flat derived tensors the induced equivalence $D(C_B)$ has the coherent tensor comparison computed by those total-complex maps on corresponding K-flat resolutions. No finiteness, nonzero-ring, enough-points or terminal-object hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The normalized ordinary braided structure is supplied by [lem-sfb-constant-restriction-ordinary-monoidal], whose ordinary_exists is constructed by sectionwise lax braided restriction, monoidal sheafification and transport, with inverse tensorator obtained by local scalar descent and the tensor universal property. Prove additivity sectionwise. Obtain the equivalence from [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]; identify the RingCat and CommRingCat presentations through constantCommuteCompose and explicit cancellation isomorphisms for scalar restriction. Exactness follows because an equivalence preserves limits and colimits [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits].

Reuse the general cochainBraided construction from the proof module of [lem-sfb-ring-isomorphism-tensor-transport] for the existing canonical termwise tensorator. Its braiding equation is checked after every total-complex coproduct injection. In bidegree (p,q), both paths apply the ordinary braided equation and multiply by the same integer sign; additivity preserves that sign. Thus the braided structure uses exactly the existing complex monoidal structure. Flatness is invariant under a strong monoidal equivalence and its inverse; identify the explicit site tensor with the monoidal tensor using [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-monoidal-equivalence-total-kflat] to obtain preservation and reflection of the acyclic test and the native two-sided K-flat test, including both tensor orders. The countable tensor-colimit hypotheses on fixed sheaves follow from [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and closedness and symmetry supply them on module sheaves. Transport the functorial flat cover along the equivalence: its augmentation is the mapped original augmentation followed by the counit, so it is natural and epimorphic.

Use the existing exact-functor localization and its equivalence instance [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Work with abstract coefficient categories to retain independent universes. Name the canonical complex and derived monoidal instances once, so compatibility definitions retain their exact existing tensor data without repeating large instance expressions. The native derived monoidal structures [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] have invertible tensor counits when the right complex is K-flat; [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] supplies invertibility of the unit and the canonical localization lax braiding. Functorial flat covers and exact integer-indexed colimits supply the existing cochain K-flat derivability instance. Choose a left resolution in this derivability structure to obtain a K-flat representative of every derived object. Apply [lem-pur-u2-normalized-braided-localization] to the source localization, target localization, canonical termwise braided functor and exact-derived factorization. It supplies a braided strong monoidal structure whose factorization is monoidal. Cancel the source and target strong tensor maps in the monoidality equation to obtain exactly the recorded cotensor square, with the inverse canonical mapCochainComplex tensorator. The braided equation, after cancellation of its tensorator, is the required equation for the independently fixed native braidings. The unit monoidality equation is precisely the recorded regular-unit normalization. The onDerived name is a regular definition with the same mapDerivedCategory body, which prevents instance registration from expanding the entire derived-functor construction.
